news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire reports 67 vacant surplus former operational assets against a portfolio of 549
news_drafts.lead:
Aberdeenshire Council had 67 vacant surplus former operational assets at the first quarter of 2026/27, according to the Business Services performance report for the Business Services Committee. Its operational portfolio, the buildings and sites it still uses, stands at 549 at the second quarter.

The paper says the number of vacant assets is expected to fall in 2026/27 and 2027/28. A number of closures are planned for early 2027, linked to a new depot and office facility at One Harlaw Road, Inverurie. The performance target for capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is 100% of the amount budgeted.

The committee also has the Business Services budget risk register for 2026/27. It identifies a pressure on income from licensing fees and charges. In the register's words, "Pressure has been identified within Licensing fees and charges however this is currently being offset with underspends across the wider Business Services budget." The risk score for council tax and fees-and-charges collection remains at 16, unchanged, with a residual score of 12.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

findings.headline: Crown Estate Scotland allocation of £919,260 placed in an earmarked reserve, with project delivery due by 31 March 2028
findings.detail: The paper says the Scottish Government now provides the allocation through General Revenue Grant rather than as a specific grant. Retaining funds beyond 31 March 2027 now requires explicit Council approval.
findings.matters: A change in how a grant is paid, and the conditions attached to retaining it, affects how other councils treat similar coastal or specific allocations.
findings.figures: £919,260 allocation; project allocations by 30 September 2027; delivery by 31 March 2028
findings.quote: Expenditure and project delivery to be completed by 31 March 2028.

findings.headline: Of eleven strategic risks reported in February 2026, nine remain High after existing controls
findings.detail: The paper groups the nine high residual risks into five themes, including financial sustainability, economic volatility, capital and asset resilience, demand and service pressures, and financial exposure.
findings.matters: The count of residual high risks after controls is a direct indicator of how much the council's exposure has moved since budget setting.
findings.figures: 11 strategic risks in February 2026; 9 remaining High after controls
findings.quote: nine remain High after existing controls

findings.headline: Integration Joint Board forecasts a £1.854m underspend for 2026/27, while council social care forecasts a £0.212m overspend
findings.detail: The paper says Adult Community Care is overspending by £2.521m and that no variance in the Council's contribution to the IJB is currently forecast. It describes the IJB position as sensitive to care demand, recruitment and prescribing costs.
findings.matters: Health and social care partnership positions are a common source of exposure for councils, and a finance director elsewhere will want to see how an IJB underspend sits alongside a service-level overspend.
findings.figures: £1.854m IJB underspend; £0.212m council social care overspend; £2.521m Adult Community Care overspend; £2.066m NHS Grampian underspends

findings.headline: Second Homes Council Tax income forecast £1.281m lower in the HRA
findings.detail: The paper notes that lower financing charges of £1.9m offset this within the HRA, which is forecast balanced overall.
findings.matters: Second homes income is a specific tax-base exposure that other councils with similar housing markets will want to compare.
findings.figures: £1.281m lower forecast income; £1.9m lower financing charges
findings.quote: £1.281m lower forecast Second Homes Council Tax income

findings.headline: Transformation Reserve balance is £28.186m, after £4.005m repaid in 2025/26 and net utilisation of £12.151m
findings.detail: The paper says the reserve is not cash-backed, so spending requires cash funding through treasury arrangements, and that £2.838m is held in the Payback Reserve and unavailable for distribution.
findings.matters: A reserve that is not cash-backed and carries a repayment obligation is a point finance directors elsewhere will check when assessing how transformation spend is funded.
findings.figures: £28.186m balance; £2.838m Payback Reserve; £12.151m net utilisation; £4.005m repaid in 2025/26

daily_post.headline: A new tactical risk for Public Local Inquiries, scored 4 x 4 with residual risk 12, was added after budget setting.
daily_post.lead: A council whose planning inquiry costs were not in its budget can show that the exposure was added mid-year, which other councils may face through the same planning process.
